intro.title: Routing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web server using Express that responds to different URL paths, like '/home' and '/about', with custom messages. You'll learn the core concept of routing, which directs incoming HTTP requests to the appropriate handler functions based on the request's URL and method. The main technologies involved are the Express framework and its built-in routing methods, such as app.get() and app.post(). By the end, you'll understand how to define routes and send responses, forming the foundation for building more complex web applications.
intro.usecase: Routing is fundamental to every web application built with Express, determining how the server responds to client requests for different URLs. In e-commerce sites, routing handles product pages, shopping carts, and checkout processes—each with its own endpoint. Content management systems use routing to serve articles, user profiles, and admin panels from distinct paths. As a developer, you'll implement routing to organize your application's structure, manage user navigation, and ensure the right content loads for each page request.
